scope: Decision point 1 (BABY_MOVE) in zdp (java/bots/zdp). Covered: the code path from open through mask, pick and executor to fallback, the use of every option in cpi-x0 (rl-m2 v39, 256 self-play games, 622,495 BABY_MOVE records), the input features, what couples the point to Nav/errand state and to other points, and a proposal to generalize the action space. The deviation and fallback-given-deviation figures come from devfb.py on a 300k-row subsample, so subsample counts are multiplied by about 2.075 to compare with full-data counts. Pick counts and per-option fallback rates come from rl_train's option_hist over all rows. I only read files and ran small local scripts (net-v2 shape check, config listing). I ran no games and no builds and did not access the VM.

points.name: BABY_MOVE
points.locations: Opens at java/bots/zdp/Baby.java:187-189 when the rat is movement-ready. Features: D.babyMove at D.java:243-325. Bookkeeping: netBook at Baby.java:2213-2221. Mask: netAllowed at Baby.java:2251-2306. Pick: Baby.java:2196, which calls D.pick (D.java:203-209), which calls DNet.sample (DNet.java:116-135; the floor is spread as floor/m at 130). Executor: netExec at Baby.java:2309-2463, plus netMineBlock at 2470-2489. Fallback: Baby.java:2202-2205 runs moveDecision (1002-1101) and sets label 0x8000|(k<<6)|zdb. The flag is set at D.java:158-162 and the record is emitted at D.java:174-181. Option constants: D.java:52-66.
points.option_kind: Mixed. Options 0-38 are branches of zdb's moveDecision cascade, numbered in its priority order (D.java:52-59). Each branch chooses its own target, applies zdb's thresholds, and drives Nav, which keeps state across turns. Options 39-71 are primitive actions: step, turn, hold, strafe and risky step (D.java:61-66). They were added so the net can make any move, and zdb never labels them.

options.name: M_GRAB
options.executor: Returns false (Baby.java:2312).
options.cannot_act_when: Always.
options.context_dependence: Dead index. moveDecision never labels it (1002-1101).

options.name: M_CAT_DEFEND
options.executor: approachCat(cat) (2313-2315, body at 1454-1471). Holds if already next to the cat's 2x2 body and outside its lane; otherwise Nav.goTo the nearest open off-lane tile around the body.
options.cannot_act_when: No open off-lane tile exists around the cat (1468).
options.context_dependence: The cascade takes it first, but only when the cat is within dist2 36 of one of our kings (1008; catAtKing 1448-1452; Cfg.CAT_DEFEND_R2 at Cfg.java:153). As an option it is offered for any visible cat. It runs the same executor as 22 and as goCat's visible-cat case.

options.name: M_END_CAT
options.executor: goCat() (2316-2318, body at 1417-1423). approachCat if a cat is visible, else Nav.goTo(knownCat()).
options.offered_when: A cat is visible, or one is known (2260). knownCat counts the rat's own sighting under 10 rounds old or a comms cat under 30 rounds old (1431-1444).
options.cannot_act_when: Only when approachCat fails.
options.context_dependence: The option skips all of endCat's gates (1407-1414). In the cascade it runs only at war from round 1850 (1010-1012), with raw < 30, not carrying, no threatened king, no enemy within dist2 8, no form or cash site, and either 2+ kings or a bank below endCatBar. As an option it means 'go to the cat' at any time, which duplicates 1, 22 and 27.

options.name: M_FLEE_CAT
options.executor: Nav.flee(cat.location) (2319-2321, body at Nav.java:220-242). Steps in whichever of 5 away directions most increases distance from the cat's centre. It checks canMove only, so it ignores Nav.avoid (Nav.java:237).
options.cannot_act_when: None of the 5 directions is movable and increases the distance (Nav.java:236-241).
options.context_dependence: The cascade uses it only for GATHER rats within catDist4 <= 80 (1014-1016). As an option it is offered to any role at any distance.

options.name: M_YIELD_KING
options.executor: yieldKing() (2322-2324, body at 1356-1370). Steps off the cat lane to a tile at least Chebyshev 3 from the nearest king.
options.cannot_act_when: Acts only when the rat is exactly Chebyshev 2 from a king, King.catGap <= 3 (1358), and an off-lane movable tile exists (1362-1369).
options.context_dependence: Not in moveDecision, so zdb never labels it and it is picked only through the floor.

options.name: M_AIM_CARRY
options.executor: aimCarry() (2325-2329, body at 583-635). Tries staying put and the 8 steps with each facing, to throw the carried enemy at an enemy within Chebyshev 3 (or a king within 4) through a free first flight tile. It turns, moves and throws (633).
options.cannot_act_when: No enemy target in range (589-602), no valid step and flight tile (630), or the rat cannot turn (631). The Flow.left() < 7000 bytecode guard (585) never binds while limits are off (Flow.java:45; patches/local-research.patch:19).
options.context_dependence: The cascade also requires !coop (1018). The option performs an act-point action (the throw) inside a move option. No feature carries target positions or flight tiles.
options.observed: 2,001 picks, 20.1% fallback (~403, of which ~285 at the argmax). 101 subsample deviations, 56% fell back.

options.name: M_RESCUE
options.executor: Returns false (2330).
options.cannot_act_when: Always.
options.context_dependence: Dead (Cfg.RESCUE is off).

options.name: M_AMMO_AWAY
options.executor: ammoAway() (2331-2333, body at 1373-1385). Nav.flee away from our nearest king.
options.offered_when: An enemy is nearest and a king exists (2265).
options.cannot_act_when: Acts only if hp <= 50, the enemy has more hp, the enemy is within dist2 8, and the rat is within Chebyshev 3 of the king (1383-1385; Cfg.java:97).
options.context_dependence: Not in moveDecision; picked only through the floor.

options.name: M_RETREAT
options.executor: retreat() (2334-2336, body at 1387-1393). Nav.goTo the nearest king.
options.offered_when: A king exists and an enemy is within dist2 20 (2266).
options.cannot_act_when: hp > 40 (Cfg.java:92), or the rat is already within Chebyshev 2 of the king (1388-1390).
options.context_dependence: The cascade requires !coop and tries it right after AIM_CARRY (1020).
options.observed: 3,594 picks, 3.6% fallback (~128, ~86 at the argmax). 43 subsample deviations, 47% fell back.

options.name: M_HUNGRY
options.executor: Alias of deliver (2337-2339).
options.cannot_act_when: n/a
options.context_dependence: Dead alias of 23.

options.name: M_FORM_KING
options.executor: formKing() (2340-2342, body at 1535-1559). Walks into the formation site's 3x3, steps onto the centre if it is free, and calls becomeRatKing there (1543, 1554).
options.offered_when: A fresh formSite is in the king's comms (2268; formSite 1528-1532).
options.cannot_act_when: dist2 to the site > 72 (Cfg.java:44; check at 1539), or outside the 3x3 with 8 or more allies nearer (Cfg.java:58; check at 1540).
options.context_dependence: The cascade tries it after the cat, flee, aim and retreat branches (1021). The option can turn the rat into a king inside a move decision.
options.observed: 8,145 picks, 0.6% fallback (~50). 19 subsample deviations, 42% fell back.

options.name: M_CASH
options.executor: cashMove() (2343-2345, body at 1697-1713). Walks into the cash site's 3x3 and holds.
options.cannot_act_when: Chebyshev distance to the site > 8 (Cfg.CASH_PULL at Cfg.java:241; check at 1699).

options.name: M_RAID, M_RAID_FIGHT
options.executor: raid() for both (2346-2349, body at 1735-1750). Keeps raidTarget or picks a new one with pickRaid (1753-1768): an enemy-half mine with G.rand spread, else the midpoint. It clears Nav.guard (1742), then goTo, or wanders once within Chebyshev 2.
options.cannot_act_when: Never; pickRaid always returns a location.
options.context_dependence: The two options are duplicates. The cascade runs RAID for a raider when !coop, raw == 0, hp >= 60, on our half and no enemy within dist2 8 (1027-1028), and RAID_FIGHT for a FIGHT raider with hp >= 60 (1062). Only the net's roleSet ever sets raider (1911-1915), so zdb never labels either option and both are picked only through the floor. Either one writes raidTarget/raidSince and Nav.guard and consumes G.rand.

options.name: M_FLANK
options.executor: flank(seen) (2350-2352, body at 1312-1337). Strafes (with Nav.guard on the enemy) onto a free, non-avoided tile next to an enemy baby within dist2 8 that the enemy cannot see. sees() uses the enemy's facing (1303-1309). The aim is for the post-move carry to grab that enemy.
options.offered_when: An enemy is nearest, the action cooldown is ready, and the rat is not carrying (2271).
options.cannot_act_when: No enemy baby within dist2 8, or every adjacent tile is seen by it, avoided or blocked (1318-1330). The mask checks neither condition, and no feature carries enemy facing.
options.context_dependence: The cascade requires !coop and tries it after RAID (1030). Its payoff depends on the post-move carry (tryCarry at 215 or the BABY_ACT_POST net).
options.observed: 725 picks, 68% fallback (~496). About 631 of the picks are deviations (304 in the subsample, 70% fell back). Argmax picks still fall back about 60% of the time.

options.name: M_PRESS
options.executor: pressKing() (2353-2355, body at 1165-1186). goTo a fresh enemy-king sighting, and turn toward its 3x3 once within Chebyshev 2.
options.offered_when: The enemy king is visible, or lastEKing is at most 8 rounds old (2272).
options.cannot_act_when: hp < 40; a GATHER rat holding raw >= 30; dist2 > 100 (> 20 for gatherers); or the sighting turns out empty, which also clears lastEKing (1168-1174).
options.context_dependence: Not in moveDecision; picked only through the floor. Its gates depend on role.

options.cannot_act_when: Presumably when no enemy baby is within dist2 20 or movement is not ready (Micro.java:18); not confirmed beyond line 30.
options.context_dependence: Not in moveDecision; picked only through the floor.

options.executor: faceEnemy() (2359-2361, body at 1226-1242). Turns to the nearest enemy within dist2 8; once facing it, steps forward if dist2 > 2 and the step is free.
options.cannot_act_when: Never, once offered.
options.context_dependence: The cascade requires !coop and either role != GATHER or an adjacent enemy (1033). It comes ahead of STALL_CAT, ATTACK and WAR, so in zdb it takes every non-gatherer turn with an enemy within dist2 8.

options.name: M_ATK_DELIVER
options.executor: Alias of deliver (2362-2363).
options.cannot_act_when: n/a
options.context_dependence: Dead alias of 23.

options.offered_when: An ATTACK rat in coop with catHunt latched (2276). Its tracker, stallTick (293-301), runs every turn in netBook (2214).
options.cannot_act_when: Never, once offered.
options.context_dependence: The cascade runs it as stallCat (1034).

options.name: M_ATTACK
options.executor: attack() (2368-2370, body at 1189-1202). goTo the visible enemy king, else the last sighting if under 30 rounds old, else the nearest live mirror spot (rushTarget 1204-1220).
options.cannot_act_when: Every mirror spot is marked noKing. rushTarget then resets noKing and returns null (1218).
options.context_dependence: The cascade runs it only for the ATTACK role (1035). As an option any role, gatherers included, can rush. It writes lastEKing, lastEKingRound and noKing whatever the role.

options.name: M_WAR
options.executor: war() (2371-2373, body at 1245-1291): four behaviours behind one index. For GATHER: turn to face an adjacent enemy. With a visible enemy king: goTo it. With an enemy at dist2 <= 2: turn to face it. With an enemy at dist2 <= 20: hold and face (the standoff) if it sees us and has at least our hp, else goTo it. Otherwise: goTo the alert location.
options.offered_when: An enemy is nearest, the enemy king is visible, our king is threatened, or an alert is fresh (2278). This includes coop turns, through the enemy king or the alert.
options.cannot_act_when: A GATHER rat that is not hunting, with no threatened king and no adjacent enemy (1249-1251). Otherwise: the enemy-king branch needs FIGHT or raw < 30 (1256); the enemy branch needs dist2 <= 2, or dist2 <= 20 together with FIGHT, raw < 30 or dist2 <= 8 (1262-1268); the alert branch needs 8 < dist2 <= 225 (1283-1285).
options.context_dependence: Behaviour depends on role, raw cheese, hunting and distances. The cascade requires !coop and runs war only after FACE (1033, 1037), so in zdb the close-range standoff code (1262-1278) rarely runs for non-gatherers. When the net picks WAR, it runs in exactly those states.
options.observed: 16,055 picks, 6.9% fallback (~1,108, the largest source; ~786 at the argmax). 454 subsample deviations, 34% fell back.

options.cannot_act_when: Never, once offered.

options.cannot_act_when: Never.

options.cannot_act_when: The rat holds new mines but has news already or no king; seek then sets mineTarget=null and seekUntil=0 before returning false (1877). Or exploreHome finds no unseen home-half tile among 12 samples (1880-1882), after it has drawn 24 G.rand numbers (1816-1817).

options.observed: 56,184 picks, 0.61% fallback (~343, ~333 at the argmax). 71 subsample deviations, 7% fell back.

Then, for GATHER/FIGHT rats, the idle tick with its shiftMine re-pick (2473-2477). Then a seek if one can start (2475, 2480), else wander at the mine or walk to it.

points.fallback_explanation:
How a fallback happens: netMove runs the chosen option's executor. If the executor returns false or throws, zdb's moveDecision runs in the same turn, and the label becomes 0x8000|(k<<6)|zdb_label (Baby.java:2193-2207). D.fallback turns that bit into the record's fallback flag (D.java:158-162).

Size: 0.43% of all 622,495 picks (~2,676). The rate is low because the net is a saturated copy of the cascade: its mean top-choice probability is 0.9928. Its top choice is usually the branch zdb would take in that state, and that branch's conditions hold.

Fallback concentrates on deviations: 13.0% of deviations fall back, against 0.28% of top choices. The deviation rate is 1.19% and the real (non-fallback) deviation rate 1.04%. Most deviations come from the 0.005 floor.

Cause: for several options the mask is looser than the executor's own preconditions, and no feature exposes those preconditions.
- FLANK: the mask lacks 'enemy baby within dist2 8' and 'an adjacent tile it cannot see'; enemy facing is not a feature.
- WAR: the mask is any enemy, enemy king, threatened king or alert, while war() is gated by role, raw cheese, hunting and distance.
- AIM_CARRY: the mask lacks 'target within Chebyshev 3' and 'free flight tile'.
- RETREAT: the mask lacks hp <= 40 and Chebyshev > 2.
- YIELD_KING and AMMO_AWAY: the mask lacks almost every condition, so they fall back 100% of the time.
- FORM_KING: distance and crowd checks.
- ATTACK: noKing exhausted.
- SEEK and MINE_EXPLORE: success depends on random samples of unseen home tiles.
- FLEE_CAT: all away directions blocked.

By source: WAR ~1,108 (~786 at the argmax), FLANK ~496 (70% of its deviations and ~60% of its argmax picks), AIM_CARRY ~403, SEEK ~343, RETREAT ~128, ATTACK ~99, FORM_KING ~50, FLEE_CAT ~34. Primitives never fall back, because their masks (2298-2305) match their executor guards (2437-2460).

Consequences:
1. rl_train keeps fallback records and gives the credit to the chosen k; the flag is only a diagnostic (rl_train.py:525-542, flag read at 538). This is valid for the MDP, since choosing k in that state does produce zdb's move. But k's effect then switches between its own behaviour and zdb's on a condition the net cannot see, so the value learned for k mixes two behaviours.
2. Some executors change state before failing, so the fallback is not exactly what zdb would have done. seek() clears mineTarget and seekUntil (1877, 1881). exploreHome() draws from G.rand (1816-1817). flank and yieldKing can turn before a failed step (Nav.java:119-126).
3. For FLANK and AIM_CARRY, most of the exploration the floor spends on that option ends up running zdb's move instead.

Point 1 is not trainable in any RL or ES config (configs/es-*.json and rl-*.json train [5,7,10,11,12,13,16], [5,7,10,11,12,13] or [11]). Today, therefore, this only affects the data the other points learn from.
points.context_dependence:
What an option does depends on much more than its index.

1. Role. war() branches on GATHER, FIGHT, hunting and raw cheese (1249-1268). pressKing gates on GATHER and raw (1169-1171). The mine block ticks only for GATHER/FIGHT (2473-2480). STALL_CAT's mask requires ATTACK in coop (2276). The cascade limits FIGHT_CAT, KNOWN_CAT and RAID_FIGHT to FIGHT (1040, 1059-1062), ATTACK to the ATTACK role (1035), SEEK to GATHER (1075) and SCOUT to scouts (1064). Most of these options are offered to every role, so a pick can run code in a role zdb never ran it in: ATTACK for a gatherer, the mine block for an attacker, SCOUT for a fighter.

2. Coop. nearestEnemy is null in coop (92-100), so the enemy options mostly drop out of the mask. WAR stays offered through the enemy king or an alert (2278). The cascade also requires !coop for AIM_CARRY, RETREAT, RAID, FLANK, FACE and WAR (1018-1037).

3. Cascade order. Each zdb label was produced only after every earlier branch failed, so the net learned option k only inside that region. Picked outside it, k's executor runs in states zdb never ran it in:
   - WAR with an enemy within dist2 8, where zdb takes FACE for non-gatherers (1033 comes before 1037);
   - DELIVER with 1 raw cheese, where the cascade needs 30, or 10 with no cheese target, or late game (1044);
   - CAT_DEFEND or END_CAT away from any king or before round 1850 (1008, 1010-1012).

4. Errand state the features see only in part: Nav.target, bugging, stall and bestDist; exploreTarget; mineTarget, mineShift and the idle counter; the seek window; raidTarget and raidSince; lastEKing and noKing; cheeseTarget; catHunt. The same index either continues an errand or starts a new one depending on this state. Choosing another target for one turn wipes Nav's progress toward the old one (Nav.java:74-79).

5. States only the net creates. The raider feature (D.java:275) was always 0 in zdb data, because only roleSet sets it (1911-1915). train_dp gives a constant column unit scale (train_dp.py:120-121), so its first-layer weights receive no gradient and stay at their random values. A net-made raider (R_RAIDER was picked 8,043 times at point 5 in cpi-x0) therefore shifts the BABY_MOVE logits by untrained weights. RAID and RAID_FIGHT are picked only through the floor, so the cascade's raider branches (1027, 1062) run for such a rat only on fallback turns.
coupling: Nav state is shared by every walking option. Nav.goTo resets bugging, bestDist and stall whenever the target changes (Nav.java:74-79), and Flow paths are requested per target (Nav.java:85, 92-97). A one-turn switch to another target throws away the bug walk and the progress counters of the errand it returns to.

Give-up thresholds read Nav.stall. chaseCheese drops its target at stall > 12 (1117). goMine drops its mine at > 25 (1137-1140). raid re-picks at > 20 (1736). explore and exploreHome re-sample at > 20 (1785, 1814). wanderAround re-samples at > 6 (1773). The trap-risk avoid mask applies only while stall < 8 (118). P_STEP deliberately leaves stall unchanged (2451-2452).
explore, exploreHome and wanderAround share exploreTarget (1773-1776, 1785-1799, 1814-1824). idleSeek, startSeek (1856, 1867) and roleExec (1900) reset it.

Mine and seek state: mineTarget, minesAtPick and mineShift (1122-1141, 1493); the idle counter, which advances only when the mine block runs (1842-1847, 2473); and the seek window (1832-1834, 1850-1869). Options 31 and 32 change this state (1877, 1881, 2416).

MINE_PICK (point 7) opens as BABY_MOVE's secondary point only inside pickMine (1494-1498). It is reached through refreshMine, shiftMine or a goMine re-pick, from options 33, 34, 36 and 37 or from the cascade.

BABY_ROLE (point 5) feeds this point in four ways. role, scout and raider are features (D.java:247, 275-276). They enter the masks (2276, 2291-2292). They switch executor code (war 1249-1268, pressKing 1169-1171, netMineBlock 2473-2480, scouting 1807-1809). And roleExec resets errand state when the role changes (1899-1906).

Effects on later points in the same turn. The why character becomes a BABY_ACT_POST feature (Baby.java:200; D.java:344). A turn spent at BABY_MOVE stops BABY_FACE from opening (228-229). Whether the rat moved gates the hard-coded drop and throw after the move (209-213). FLANK pays off only through the post-move carry (215 or the BABY_ACT_POST net). AIM_CARRY throws (633), CHEESE_PICK picks up (1108) and FORM_KING can promote to king (1543, 1554), all inside a move option.
King-side inputs: formSite, from the king's comms, gates FORM_KING (1528-1532), and cashSite gates CASH. COURIER and SCOUT_HOME trips exist to carry mine news to a king (1046, 1065).

Enemy-king memory: attack() and netBook write lastEKing, lastEKingRound and noKing for any role that takes ATTACK (1190-1218, 2213-2221). pressKing clears lastEKing (1174). These feed features 25-26 and PRESS's mask (2272).
Nav.guard: flank sets it and restores it (1331-1334), and raid clears it for good (1742). Nav.step turns toward the guard while stepping (Nav.java:115-118), which changes strafing and later facing.

The G.rand stream is consumed by explore (1794), exploreHome (1817), wanderAround (1774) and pickRaid (1763), so choosing these options shifts zdb's random draws elsewhere. Net sampling uses DNet's separate streams (DNet.java:84-103).

Nav.avoid holds the cat lanes, plus the trap-risk mask outside coop and engagement (118; TrapRisk.java:55-71). It masks steps in Nav.free (Nav.java:66-69) and the primitive masks, but Nav.flee ignores it (Nav.java:237).
points.proposal_cost:
Stage 1: about 200-300 Java lines (can-act checks, the war split and the bookkeeping move in Baby.java; feature changes in D.java). Option-table changes in scripts/dp_points.py and decisions.py. New zdb imitation data and a train_dp run for point 1, then a 128-256-game check against zdb. About 1-2 days.

Stage 2 with fixed slots: about 400-600 Java lines, split roughly as candidate generators and slot features ~200, executor modes ~80, the micro point (open, mask, executor, features) ~150, label instrumentation in moveDecision ~60 and commitment ~40. About 100 Python lines (new point registration and label decoding), plus the data collection, imitation and check runs. About 3-5 days. A shared per-candidate scorer would add about 300-400 Python lines (variable-length candidate records through rl_data, dpnet_io, train_dp, rl_train and build_dpnet) and about 60 Java lines in DNet.

Risks:
- Imitation fidelity of the target head: zdb's priority logic has to be recoverable from the candidate features. Measure per-type label accuracy before RL.
- Input size: slots enlarge the input. Bytecodes are not limited now; tournament limits would need a separate budget pass.
- Nav state: switching targets resets the bug and flow state (Nav.java:74-79), so CONTINUE or commitment is needed to avoid thrashing.
- G.rand use changes, so there is no bit-exact zdb replay. The user has allowed this.
points.missing_information:
- I did not compute per-option allowed rates or a breakdown of fallbacks by role or coop. The masks in cpi-x0's p1.npz would give both with a short script on the VM.
- Point 1's sensitivity run (plan section 16, item 2: zdph1 with floor 0.2 against v39, 64 games) has no results yet, so I cannot say whether point-1 deviations are costly or nearly free.
- I did not read the point-1 weights of v39 or the m2 start net; they are not local. The zero comms columns and the bias -20 primitive rows are inferred from widen's documentation and the rl-m2 config. Only net-v2's point 1 (60-64-64-39) was checked.
- The size of the logit shift from the untrained raider column was not measured.
- The turns lost to Nav resets after a one-turn target switch were not measured.
- I did not check whether fallbacks cluster by map or game phase.
- I re-read only lines 16-30 of Micro.act in this pass.
- The 2.075 scale between the devfb subsample and the full data assumes the 300k-row subsample is uniform.

cross_cutting: rl_train trains on fallback records and credits the chosen option, at every cascade-branch point (rl_train.py:525-542; the flag is set at D.java:158-162 and is only a diagnostic). Either make each mask equal to its executor's success condition, or drop or relabel fallback records in the policy loss.

Widened options start with zero weights and bias -20, and widened input columns start at zero (docs/decision-points.md:189-190; configs/rl-m2.json:3). On a frozen point (1, and others not in the trainable lists) these options are pure floor noise with logits that ignore the state, and the comms features are invisible. On a trainable point they learn only from floor samples, about floor/m per decision.

Features that were constant in zdb data, such as raider (D.java:275), keep their random first-layer weights (train_dp.py:120-121; unmasked cross-entropy at train_dp.py:132). States only the net creates, like an R_RAIDER role from point 5, then shift every point that reads them by untrained weights. Zero those columns at export.

Advantages are the team's game outcome minus a team-state baseline over 10-round bins (rl_train.py:25, 35-39). Per-turn movement decisions (about 1,200 per team per game at point 1) are nearly unidentifiable from that signal. Movement needs coarser decisions in time (commit to a target, decide on events), or per-rat signals.
Hard-coded actions after the move when BABY_ACT_POST's net does not act (Baby.java:209-226): drop ally, throw, carry, bite enemies, bite the cat, layLane in coop, and tryDeliver.

Research games run with bytecode limits off: getBytecodeLimit returns 1e9 (patches/local-research.patch:19), so Flow.left() is huge (Flow.java:45) and guards on it, such as aimCarry's 7000 check (585), never bind. By arithmetic estimate (not measured), point 1's 76-64-64-72 MLP alone is about 13.5k multiply-adds per call, which would not fit the 17,500-bytecode baby limit (RobotPlayer.java:33). Behaviour under tournament limits would therefore differ.

Cascade-branch options assume they run where zdb ran them: after every earlier branch failed, and inside zdb's role and coop gates. Any point whose options are cascade branches has the same problem: when the net picks an option outside that region, the executor runs in states zdb never visited. The fix that carries over to every point is role-free options with exact masks and features that describe each alternative.
MINE_PICK already shows a pattern the other movement-like points can reuse: choosing among ranked candidates through fixed slots with per-slot features (D.java:99-100, 822-852; Baby.java:1494-1498).
